subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static pickup truck model around 5.4m long, skipping rig joints since it's not a creature, and deciding to make it hover slightly above the ground with thrusters rather than sitting flush on the floor.

Instead I'll add four short landing struts so the lowest points rest right on y=0, with the hover thruster pods positioned near the wheel locations. I'm laying out the build using boxes for the chassis, extrusions for the cab's side profile, and lathes for the thrusters, plus SVG textures for decals, headlights, a star emblem, stripes, and a license plate, and now I'm working out exact coordinates for the chassis and cab geometry along the truck's length.

Shaping the cab profile...

Figuring out the windshield tilt direction and offset to keep it flush with the cab slope. Now I'm planning the militarized add-ons: side armor plates, a roof turret/gun rack in the bed, bull bar, roll cage, antenna, spotlights, neon underglow strips, and hover thruster pods with glowing cyan discs at each wheel well.

Working out the hover pod geometry and placement — positioning the cylindrical pods with glow discs at the wheel arches, connecting them to the chassis with support arms, and sizing them so they slightly overlap the body bottom without clipping through it.

Adding small cylindrical feet at the outer edges of each pod down to the ground, then shaping the pod shroud as a lathe profile with a glow disc underneath and a fan texture plane on top.

I'm designing a bottom-facing glow disc with a concentric-ring radial gradient texture for the pod underside, then adding door emblem decals with star/hex graphics and "UNIT 07" text, positioning them as planes on each side of the cab facing outward.

Working through the axis orientation math to make sure the decal text reads correctly from a viewer standing outside each door, since the local coordinate system needs to be mirrored properly on the opposite sides so the text doesn't appear flipped.

Now I'm planning the detail elements: glowing headlight strips in cyan-white, a dark grille with slat textures, a bull bar made of tubes, and a yellow-black chevron bumper, plus red taillight glows at the rear. For the body finish I'm thinking matte olive-black military paint with cyberpunk magenta/cyan accents, using procedural noise-based weathering that adds mud near the bottom and panel-line wear, along with camo patches layered on top of the base paint.

On top I'm adding a roof rack with a sensor dome, antenna rods with glowing tips, and a spotlight bar, plus a rotating bed turret with twin cylindrical barrels and an ammo box, all built from rod and cylinder primitives in model space. I'm also sketching out large rear thruster nozzles mounted at the back of the bed.

Now I'm layering on surface details: glowing magenta strip boxes along the lower sides, a thin cyan stripe, a number plate, small mirror arms, door seam lines, and simple angular armor plates over the wheel pods in place of fender flares, keeping rivets to a few merged boxes for simplicity.

I'll build reusable helpers—a box-part function and a mirror helper to duplicate parts left and right—and skip joints since static models don't need bones. Then I'll plan out the texture set: grille, emblem, hazard chevrons, plate, fan, taillight strip, and a glowing side decal reading "HOVER-7" rendered as SVG text.

I'm sizing the overall truck: roughly 1.95 height plus a 2.4 antenna, 5.3 length, with the glass panel using a dark flat color and slight emissive glow. Now I'm working out the extrusion geometry for the cab shape, centering the outline thickness around the origin so it spans evenly on both sides.

For the hood, I'm shaping its sloped profile and adding scoop/vent details with glowing slits, calculating the y-height along the hood's slope at different z positions to position the vents correctly on the slanted surface.

Now I'm laying out the truck bed: a flat floor section, sidewalls as boxes flanking the bed, and a tailgate panel closing off the back end.

I'm placing a turret in the bed with a cylindrical base, a boxy housing, and forward-pointing barrel rods, adjusting the facing and height so the barrels clear the cab roof, and adding an ammo drum nearby.

Now I'm positioning side thrusters near the wheel pods and arm boxes, then modeling the rear nozzles as lathed shapes with a tapered outline, placing them under the bed near the rear bumper.

Designing the thruster pod shape, then adding a glow disc and a thin cyan/magenta ring for rim lighting, and starting to work out leg geometry attached to the pod's outer radius.

Working out the foot struts and pads positioned beneath each pod, then sketching the front bull bar as a textured box with vertical and crossbar tube elements for the bumper.

Now I'm shaping the hood front with a taller profile to fit a dark grille plane, adjusting the bumper box dimensions so the grille sits cleanly above it, and sizing headlight glow bars narrower to avoid overlapping the grille.

I'm adding a roof lightbar for the cab front, placing it above the windshield with a blend of cyan and magenta coloring, plus a small dome sensor on a roof rack. Now I'm setting up color constants, glow and geometry merge imports, and planning how textured versus plain-colored parts get applied before writing the grille texture as an SVG with dark background and vertical slats.

Still writing SVG textures...

Placing wing mirrors on cab arms, then adding door seam lines and window glass profiles with a sloped windshield line at the front of the cab.

Checking the windshield glass thickness against the front slope edge, it looks roughly flush and fine since the windshield is a separate piece. Now I'm adding armor side plates over the doors as thin boxes in olive-dark, plus considering an emblem plane placement on the plate.

Now I'm positioning the emblem relative to the plate surface, adding a magenta underglow box beneath the chassis for visibility, and planning a roof sensor rod with a glowing sphere tip plus antennas.

I'm also sketching roof details like a dish dome, light bar, rack rails, and search cylinder, plus adding glowing battery cells to the bed. Then I'm starting the paint function for the body material, blending a base color with a grime layer driven by noise and height.

Writing camo color blend...

Writing lathe and glow placement code...
